original_question: Is there a number N such that every irreducible geodesic net whose unbalanced vertices are exactly the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron has at most N balanced vertices?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.2.3 in Section 3.2: Is there a number N such that each irreducible geodesic net with unbalanced vertices at all vertices of a regular tetrahedron has at most N balanced vertices?
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly identifies the object class (irreducible geodesic nets), the prescribed unbalanced-vertex configuration (the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron), and the question of whether there is a uniform upper bound N on the number of balanced vertices.
missing_details: The ambient setting is Euclidean three-space R^3; this is a genuinely 3-dimensional boundary configuration, not a planar one.

A geodesic net must be understood in the paper's sense: a finite connected embedded graph in the ambient manifold; in Euclidean space its edges are straight geodesic segments, and edges are not allowed to intersect or self-intersect except at common endpoints.

Balanced and unbalanced vertices should be defined explicitly: at each balanced vertex, the sum of the outgoing unit tangent vectors along all incident edges is 0; the prescribed boundary points are the unbalanced vertices.

The standing conventions from Section 1.1 are important here: balanced vertices of degree 2 are excluded (otherwise one could subdivide edges indefinitely and make the number of balanced vertices arbitrarily large), the nets considered are connected, and the paper agrees to exclude edges between unbalanced vertices.

Irreducible needs its exact paper definition: no subgraph formed by a proper subset of the edges, together with all incident vertices, is itself a geodesic net with the same set of unbalanced vertices.
The quantifier on N should be explicit: N is a single universal constant, independent of the particular irreducible net, for this fixed boundary configuration.
refined_question: Does there exist a universal constant N in the natural numbers such that every finite connected embedded geodesic net in R^3, with straight-line edges, no edge intersections or self-intersections except at common endpoints, no edges joining two unbalanced vertices, and all balanced vertices of degree at least 3, whose set of unbalanced vertices is exactly the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron, and which is irreducible in the sense that no proper subset of its edges together with all incident vertices forms a geodesic net with the same four unbalanced vertices, has at most N balanced vertices?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Problem 3.2.3 in Section 3.2, not the nearby planar questions Problem 3.2.1 or Conjecture 3.2.2, because it singles out irreducible geodesic nets and the regular-tetrahedron boundary configuration. The draft already matches the official wording almost verbatim. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, the main additions are the ambient space R^3, the paper's definition of geodesic net and of balanced/unbalanced vertices from Definition 1.1.1, the standing conventions in Section 1.1 (especially exclusion of degree-2 balanced vertices, since those can be inserted arbitrarily), and the exact definition of irreducible from the paragraph immediately before Problem 3.2.1. The paper does not give an explicit equivalent reformulation of Problem 3.2.3.
